Pollution from a single identifiable location (factory pipe, oil spill).
Released directly into the environment, e.g., SO2 from coal combustion.
Formed by reaction of primary pollutants, e.g., tropospheric ozone, sulfuric acid.

Designing out waste and reusing materials.
The variety of living organisms in an area, measured at the level of genes, species and ecosystems, and an indicator of ecological health.
The protection and careful management of habitats and species to maintain biodiversity, for example through nature reserves and breeding programmes.
A community of living organisms together with the non-living physical environment, interacting as a system through energy flow and nutrient cycling.
A network of interconnected food chains showing the feeding relationships and flow of energy between organisms in a community.
A species whose presence has a disproportionately large effect on its ecosystem, so that its loss would dramatically change the community.
A feeding position in a food chain, such as producer, primary consumer or secondary consumer, through which energy passes.
